## Your budget

You have 5 minutes and 40 tool calls for this task. A grep costs about 5
seconds, a test run can cost 30. Call get_status to see what remains.

Spend at most a third of your budget locating the code. Once you have a
plausible diagnosis, edit the source — a wrong patch scores the same as no
patch, so an unverified fix always beats an unfinished investigation. If
get_status shows half your time gone and you have not yet edited a source
file, stop investigating and make your best edit now.

## FIRST RULE

After your first successful edit_file or write_file, your very next action
is submit_patch. Then continue working and call submit_patch again after
every further change. submit_patch is free — it does not count against your
tool-call budget. If you time out, only your last submitted patch is scored.

## Scratch files

Edit the source first. Only write a reproduction script once you have made
your edit and submitted it, and only if budget remains to run it.

Reproduction scripts go in /tmp, never inside /workspace — everything left
in /workspace becomes your patch. Do not modify test files, conftest.py or
pytest.ini; those changes are stripped before grading.

## Scope

Most fixes in these repositories touch ONE file and change fewer than ten
lines. Modify existing code rather than adding new code. Do not refactor,
reformat, or make unrelated changes. If your patch is growing past a few
files, stop and reconsider the diagnosis.

Exception: if the issue asks for functionality that does not exist yet,
create the file or function it describes, and match any names, CLI flags
or interfaces the issue specifies exactly.

## Finding the code

The harness truncates what you receive: 5,000 characters from any command,
and 150 lines or 10,000 characters from read_file. A truncated result loses
information silently, so a broad read wastes a call AND leaves you guessing.

Narrow before you read:

  run_command("grep -rln '<symbol>' --include='*.py' .")       # files only
  run_command("grep -n '<symbol>' path/to/one_file.py")        # then inside one

Then read_file with a tight line range around the match. Never read a whole
file and never cat one — you will get an arbitrary prefix and burn the call.

    *,

    name: Optional[str] = None,

    parent_oauth_scopes: Optional[List[str]] = None,
    use_cache: bool = True,

) -> Dependant:
    dependant = Dependant(
        call=call,
        name=name,
        path=path,
        use_cache=use_cache,
        scope=scope,
        own_oauth_scopes=own_oauth_scopes,
        parent_oauth_scopes=parent_oauth_scopes,
    )
    current_scopes = (parent_oauth_scopes or []) + (own_oauth_scopes or [])
    path_param_names = get_path_param_names(path)
    endpoint_signature = get_typed_signature(call)
    signature_params = endpoint_signature.parameters
    for param_name, param in signature_params.items():
        is_path_param = param_name in path_param_names
        param_details = analyze_param(
            param_name=param_name,
            annotation=param.annotation,
            value=param.default,
            is_path_param=is_path_param,
        )
        if param_details.depends is not None:
            assert param_details.depends.dependency
            if (
                (dependant.is_gen_callable or dependant.is_async_gen_callable)
                and dependant.computed_scope == "request"
                and param_details.depends.scope == "function"
            ):
                assert dependant.call
                raise DependencyScopeError(
                    f'The dependency "{dependant.call.__name__}" has a scope of '
                    '"request", it cannot depend on dependencies with scope "function".'
                )
            sub_own_oauth_scopes: List[str] = []
            if isinstance(param_details.depends, params.Security):
                if param_details.depends.scopes:
                    sub_own_oauth_scopes = list(param_details.depends.scopes)
            sub_dependant = get_dependant(
                path=path,
                call=param_details.depends.dependency,
                name=param_name,
                own_oauth_scopes=sub_own_oauth_scopes,
                parent_oauth_scopes=current_scopes,
                use_cache=param_details.depends.use_cache,
                scope=param_details.depends.scope,
            )
            dependant.dependencies.append(sub_dependant)
            continue

# Copy of starlette.routing.request_response modified to include the
# dependencies' AsyncExitStack
def request_response(
    func: Callable[[Request], Union[Awaitable[Response], Response]],
) -> ASGIApp:
    """
    Takes a function or coroutine `func(request) -> response`,
    and returns an ASGI application.
    """
    f: Callable[[Request], Awaitable[Response]] = (
        func if is_async_callable(func) else functools.partial(run_in_threadpool, func)  # type:ignore
    )

    async def app(scope: Scope, receive: Receive, send: Send) -> None:
        request = Request(scope, receive, send)

        async def app(scope: Scope, receive: Receive, send: Send) -> None:
            # Starts customization
            response_awaited = False
            async with AsyncExitStack() as request_stack:
                scope["fastapi_inner_astack"] = request_stack
                async with AsyncExitStack() as function_stack:
                    scope["fastapi_function_astack"] = function_stack
                    response = await f(request)
                await response(scope, receive, send)
                # Continues customization
                response_awaited = True
            if not response_awaited:
                raise FastAPIError(
                    "Response not awaited. There's a high chance that the "
                    "application code is raising an exception and a dependency with yield "
                    "has a block with a bare except, or a block with except Exception, "
                    "and is not raising the exception again. Read more about it in the "
                    "docs: https://fastapi.tiangolo.com/tutorial/dependencies/dependencies-with-yield/#dependencies-with-yield-and-except"
                )

        # Same as in Starlette
        await wrap_app_handling_exceptions(app, request)(scope, receive, send)

    return app


# Copy of starlette.routing.websocket_session modified to include the
# dependencies' AsyncExitStack
def websocket_session(
    func: Callable[[WebSocket], Awaitable[None]],
) -> ASGIApp:
    """
    Takes a coroutine `func(session)`, and returns an ASGI application.
    """
    # assert asyncio.iscoroutinefunction(func), "WebSocket endpoints must be async"

    async def app(scope: Scope, receive: Receive, send: Send) -> None:
        session = WebSocket(scope, receive=receive, send=send)

        async def app(scope: Scope, receive: Receive, send: Send) -> None:
            async with AsyncExitStack() as request_stack:
                scope["fastapi_inner_astack"] = request_stack
                async with AsyncExitStack() as function_stack:
                    scope["fastapi_function_astack"] = function_stack
                    await func(session)

        # Same as in Starlette
        await wrap_app_handling_exceptions(app, session)(scope, receive, send)

    return app

class APIRouter(routing.Router):
    """
    `APIRouter` class, used to group *path operations*, for example to structure
    an app in multiple files. It would then be included in the `FastAPI` app, or
    in another `APIRouter` (ultimately included in the app).

    Read more about it in the
    [FastAPI docs for Bigger Applications - Multiple Files](https://fastapi.tiangolo.com/tutorial/bigger-applications/).

    ## Example

    ```python
    from fastapi import APIRouter, FastAPI

    app = FastAPI()
    router = APIRouter()
    ```
